prize_parts.citation: for the development of base editing, programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand cleavage
for targeted protein degradation: the PROTAC concept and the identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide-type molecular glues

statement.case_for: Base editing remains my first choice. Cytidine and adenosine deamination, a defined chemical reaction, was made programmable and was shown to work without a double-strand break, and the evolved TadA deaminase is real enzyme chemistry. The editing outcomes have been measured carefully by many independent laboratories and the method is in clinical use. Targeted protein degradation is the second achievement I now support: a small molecule is designed to bring a ligase and a target together, and the cereblon result by Handa explains at the level of molecular mechanism why thalidomide-type drugs work. That half already has a long clinical record, which answers my own round-1 worry that no PROTAC is approved. Each part has a clear principle, independent reproduction and a citation that can be written in one line, and together they need only three names.
statement.case_against: Base editing is only about ten years old, clinical proof is still accumulating, and the Kondo and Nishida deaminase-fusion work is a real competing claim that a Liu-only citation does not settle. The 2020 CRISPR-Cas9 prize also lets some say genome editing is already honoured. For degradation, no bifunctional degrader appears to be approved, Deshaies, Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto are left out, and the PROTAC concept and the cereblon glue mechanism are two stories a single citation joins. Finally, nothing scientifically links the two parts; I accept that the pairing is a way to give each a clean attribution within three names, not a unified theme.

responses.point: A two-part prize of base editing for Liu and degradation for Crews and Handa keeps attribution clean within three names, and Komor and Gaudelli would be a serious option only if base editing were the sole part.
responses.response: I now agree with your configuration, and this is where my preferred set changes. In round 1 I wanted a one-part prize. I accept your reasoning that naming the two first-author trainees uses slots the second part needs, and that the conception and programme of both editors are Liu's. I would still say openly that Komor and Gaudelli did the decisive experiments, and that the citation should speak of base editing as a capability, not a single laboratory's result. I also share your reading that Handa's cereblon work is the part of degradation that is already medicine, which is why I accept Crews and Handa and not a third name.

responses.point: Degradation is a design principle that explains both PROTACs and molecular glues in one framework, and the glue half has an extensive clinical record, so the principle is clinically proven.
responses.response: You moved me. I put B066 third in my opening and called the missing approved PROTAC my main uncertainty, but the cereblon half of the story is measured, mechanistic and clinical, which is the kind of evidence I trust. I do not follow you to Deshaies as the third name in a prize shared with base editing, because the three-person limit across two parts leaves no room, and I would accept your own statement that Ciulli could replace him. If B066 were the only part, I would take your trio over my own two names. My remaining caution is that PROTACs and glues are not obviously one discovery, and the citation must say so honestly.

responses.point: A pairing of Buchwald and Hartwig for C-N coupling with Liu for base editing gives two distinct achievements within three names, and Liu, Komor and Gaudelli would be the defensible set for a single-achievement prize.
responses.response: I agree the mechanism of C-N coupling is clean, but my reservation stands that it extends an area honoured in 2010, and Kosugi and Migita-type precedents leave a priority question that the committee has to settle first. That is why I keep B039 as my first alternative, not a part. On the chair's question, I accept that no unifying citation links B062 to either second part. I prefer a second part that is itself new in capability, and degradation is, whereas C-N coupling is a refinement. On the base editing set, I now agree with you and Somfai that Liu alone is more defensible than a trio, and I withdraw the three-name proposal.

responses.point: Naming Komor and Gaudelli would push the union to four people with Buchwald and Hartwig, and Nobel precedent for PI-led tool development favours the group leader.
responses.response: Your precedent argument persuades me and I am dropping the trainees from my set. The remaining weakness is Kondo and Nishida: Liu alone does not resolve their independent work, and the committee should say in the citation text that the achievement is the programmable base editor, not the first deaminase-fusion. I would want the first dated demonstrations checked before the vote, since this is a matter of measurement and not of opinion.

responses.point: Condensates supply a general physical-chemical principle of cellular organisation, with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen as a coherent trio.
responses.response: I still keep B036 as an alternative and not a part. The principle of multivalent demixing is credible, but as an experimentalist I need the claim that a given condensate is liquid and functional in cells to be settled by direct measurement, and much of the evidence is indirect. I would accept the concept without agreeing that the credited set, which excludes Pappu and Mittag, is secure.

uncertainties: Whether Kondo and Nishida's independent cytidine deaminase fusion work requires shared credit or a narrower citation than Liu alone for base editing.
Whether clinical outcomes for base editing by 2026 are strong enough that recognition is mature and not premature.
Whether the PROTAC concept and cereblon glue mechanism are one discovery, and whether leaving out Deshaies and Ciulli can be defended given that no bifunctional degrader appears approved.
Whether the committee can accept a two-part prize with no scientific link, or whether the vote will favour a single achievement.
statement.conflict_note: No personal, collaborative or institutional conflict with any credited candidate. My dNTP and genome-stability work is thematically adjacent to base editing (nucleotide deamination and DNA repair) and to the ubiquitin-proteasome machinery that degraders use, but I have no collaboration with Liu, Crews or Handa. My collaborators named in my profile (Stillman, Rothstein, Thelander lineage) are not on the shortlist. This is unchanged from round 1.
